h1: The 7 Best Push-Button Start Lawn Mowers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Push-Button Start Mowers: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: seven push-button start lawn mowers, from full-size self-propelled EGO and Greenworks to small cordless 16-inch decks.
summary: The EGO Power+ LM2134SP-2 is the best push-button start lawn mower, a 21 inch self-propelled model with a push-button key start on a cordless battery platform. The Greenworks 80V gives self-propel for less with a 4.0Ah pack included, and the EGO LM2114 is the push-drive 21 inch option. The Greenworks 60V and 40V, MZK and KOMASTY serve push-mowing and small-lawn needs.
intro: A push-button start sounds like a small convenience until you stand over a gas mower on a cold morning with a sore shoulder. The trap is that battery mowers differ wildly in what ships in the box. Some sell a bare tool, some include one battery, and a few add a spare, and the sticker price tells you nothing about which you are getting.

Seven mowers made this ranking after a read of their spec pages, with battery platform, deck width, drive type and included items doing most of the work in the Primea score. Prices appear as buckets. Every pick lists a key start, so the real choice is between a full 21 inch deck, a compact 16 inch one, and whether the wheels drive themselves.

products.name: EGO Power+ 21-Inch Cordless Electric Self-Propelled Lawn Mower (LM2134SP-2)
products.verdict: Push-button key start and self-propelled drive on a full 21 inch deck.
products.description:
The EGO LM2134SP-2 has a 21-inch deck, self-propelled drive and a push-button key start on EGO's cordless battery platform, in the $500 and up bucket. Self-propel drives the wheels for you, which turns a slope or a big lawn from a chore into a walk.

It ranks first because it combines the two features this guide cares about, an easy start and a drive, on a full-width deck. The Greenworks 80V matches it on features while dropping a price tier, which makes it the value rival.

Buy it for a larger lawn where both features pay off. The caveats are the top price tier and the added weight of the drive system. Skip it if you want to spend under $500.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting push-button starting plus self-propel.

products.name: Greenworks 80V 21-Inch Self-Propelled Lawn Mower, 4.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: Self-propelled with an 80V 4.0Ah pack for less than the EGO.
products.description:
The Greenworks 80V has a 21-inch deck, self-propelled drive, a push-button key start and an 80V 4.0Ah battery plus charger in the box, in the $200 to $500 bucket. An 80V pack carries a higher voltage than the 40V and 60V models, which suits the extra load of a drive system.

It ranks second because it matches the EGO LM2134SP-2 on features while dropping into the $200 to $500 bucket, with the battery already included. You give up the EGO platform and the brand's reputation.

Buy it for self-propel at a lower price. The caveats are a different battery ecosystem and added weight. Skip it if you already own EGO batteries.
products.idealFor: Buyers wanting self-propel at a lower price.

products.name: EGO POWER+ 21-Inch Cordless Electric Lawn Mower with Battery, Charger (LM2114)
products.verdict: A 21 inch push mower on the 56V platform, battery included.
products.description:
The EGO LM2114 has a 21-inch cutting deck, a 56V battery platform, a battery and charger in the box and a push drive, in the $200 to $500 bucket. A push mower is lighter than a self-propelled one, which matters for storage and lifting.

It ranks third because it drops the self-propel of the two above, which means more effort on larger lawns. It stays on a respected platform, and the box includes everything you need.

Buy it for standard-size lawns. The caveats are no self-propel and effort on bigger yards. Skip it if you want drive assistance.

products.name: Greenworks 60V 21-Inch Push Lawn Mower, 5.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A 21 inch push deck with a 60V 5.0Ah pack included.
products.description:
The Greenworks 60V has a 21-inch deck, a 60V 5.0Ah battery with charger included, push drive and a push-button key start, in the $200 to $500 bucket. A 5.0Ah pack runs longer than a 4.0Ah one at the same voltage, which means more lawn per charge.

It ranks fourth because it offers a bigger pack than the Greenworks 80V but no self-propel. Against the EGO LM2114, it trades a respected platform for a larger battery.

Buy it for full-width push mowing without paying for self-propel. The caveats are no drive assistance and a different battery platform. Skip it if you want a self-propelled drive.
products.idealFor: Full-width push mowing without paying for self-propel.

products.name: Greenworks 40V 16-Inch Push Lawn Mower, 4.0 Ah Battery and Charger
products.verdict: A compact 16 inch push-button mower with battery included.
products.description:
The Greenworks 40V has a 16-inch deck, a 40V 4.0Ah battery and charger included, push drive and a push-button key start, in the $200 to $500 bucket. A 16 inch deck is light and slips into a small shed, which suits a townhouse lawn.

It ranks fifth because the deck is five inches narrower than the 21-inch group, though it is easier to store and handle. You make more passes, which costs time on anything bigger than a small yard.

Buy it for small lawns where compactness matters. The caveats are the narrower deck and a price above generic 16-inch models. Skip it if you have a standard-size lawn.

products.name: MZK 40V 16-Inch 2-in-1 Brushless Cordless Push Lawn Mower
products.verdict: A 16 inch brushless 2-in-1 with a push-button key start.
products.description:
The MZK has a 16-inch deck, a 40V battery platform, a brushless motor and a push-button key start, as a 2-in-1 push mower, in the $100 to $200 bucket. A brushless motor wears less than a brushed one and wastes less battery as heat.

It ranks sixth because it is from a lesser-known brand and the listing does not say what battery is included, which matters when the pack is the expensive part. It undercuts the Greenworks 40V on price.

Buy it for budget buyers with small lawns. The caveats are the unknown brand and unlisted battery details. Skip it if you want a major battery ecosystem.
products.skipIf: You want a major battery ecosystem.

products.name: KOMASTY 40V 16-Inch Cordless Battery Powered Lawn Mower, 2-in-1 Mulching
products.verdict: Two 4.0Ah batteries and two chargers at the lowest price.
products.description:
The KOMASTY has a 16-inch deck, a 40V battery platform and a push-button key start, and it includes two 4.0Ah batteries and two chargers, in the $50 to $100 bucket. It is a 2-in-1 mulching design. Two batteries mean you can swap a charged pack mid-job.

It ranks last because the brand is the least established, and a narrow deck means more passes. It is the cheapest mower here, and the spare battery doubles the runtime.

Buy it for tight budgets that want a spare battery. The caveats are the unproven brand and the narrow deck. Skip it if you prefer an established brand.
products.idealFor: Tight budgets that want a spare battery.

whatMatters.detail: A push-button key start replaces the pull cord with a safety key and a button. It matters because there is no yanking, which helps anyone with a bad shoulder or a fear of kickback. Look for push-button in the title or bullets, and check that the key must be inserted before the mower runs. A removable key also stops children starting it.

Self-propelled mowers drive their own wheels. They help on slopes and big lawns but add weight and cost. Look for the self-propelled label, and weigh whether your lawn is large or sloped enough to justify a heavier machine, because push models are easier on small yards. A drive also saves effort when the bag is full.

Volts set the power platform and amp-hours set runtime. A 5.0Ah pack runs longer than a 4.0Ah one. Check both numbers and the charger, and confirm the battery is in the box, because a bare tool listing can cost more once you add a pack. Battery cost is the main hidden expense.

A 21-inch deck covers more per pass than a 16-inch deck. A wider deck is heavier and harder to store. Match width to lawn size, and think about storage space, since a big deck needs a larger shed or garage corner. Foldable handles help in a tight space.

Some listings include a spare battery or second charger. That can change the effective price, as with the KOMASTY's two packs. Read the included items line, and compare the total value, not the sticker price alone, because the battery is often the costliest part. A spare pack doubles your mowing time.

faq.q: What is a push-button key start?
faq.a: You insert a safety key and press a button instead of pulling a cord. All seven picks list it, so the start system does not separate them. Deck, drive and included battery do.
They buy a bare tool without a battery. Check the included items before ordering, as the EGO and Greenworks listings state their batteries. The MZK listing does not, so ask before buying.
On a large or sloped lawn, yes. On a small lawn the extra weight is not worth it, and the 16 inch models stay easy to push. Slopes and wet grass are where a drive earns its cost.

faq.q: How do I set up a battery mower?
faq.a: Charge the battery, insert it, insert the key and press the button. Follow the manual's safety steps for the EGO or Greenworks model, and always remove the key before clearing a jam.
Clean the deck after use and store the battery indoors. Check the manual for blade guidance, and avoid leaving a battery in a hot shed, since heat shortens its life.
The MZK and KOMASTY are 2-in-1 designs, and the KOMASTY is listed as mulching. Check the others on their product pages, because the listing for each model may or may not mention a mulch plug.

finalTake: Buy the EGO LM2134SP-2 if you want an easy start and a drive, and the Greenworks 80V for self-propel at a lower price. The EGO LM2114 and Greenworks 60V suit standard lawns that do not need drive assistance. The 16 inch Greenworks, MZK and KOMASTY fit small yards. Confirm what is in the box, because the battery is the expensive part.
